text.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 8: Two solar inputs beat full and expanded sets; Wind5 has no established gain over original lean wind'
text.tspan: Figure 8: Two solar inputs beat full and expanded sets; Wind5 has no
established gain over original lean wind

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Power forecasts at six solar and three wind farms in National Grid Electricity Distribution's Lincolnshire trial area each contain 51 weather-driven predictions. Fair continuous ranked probability score (fair CRPS) measures their distributional error against observed power; lower is better. The comparisons match the same forecast cases and were added after the original results. Each row is the first recipe minus the second; negative means lower loss for the first. Each farm's effective capacity is the 99th percentile of absolute observed power over its available history, including readings after validation, not a connection rating. Loss is divided by that fixed scale for scoring only; one point is 1% of capacity. PV means photovoltaic. Numbers name real inputs: PV 2 uses temperature and short-wave radiation; PV 11 adds weather and solar geometry. Wind 5 uses temperature, speeds, and directions at 10/100 m. Direction is the angle the wind comes from, measured clockwise from north. Wind 9 adds eastward/northward velocity components (u/v) in m/s at both heights; Wind 7 replaces each direction angle with its sine and cosine. Full 24 is the cleaned full-input control; old lean Wind retains 16 inputs. Corrected wind/radiation processing and per-meter squared-error fitting are shared. All retained sets duplicate their own inputs to width 24. Wind representations use the same corrected polar inputs, not native upstream u/v, and add no weather information. A trains April 2024–June 2025, tests July 2025–June 2026. Retrospective B trains July 2025–June 2026, tests April 2024–June 2025; its later training conditions the comparison. Main: 500 trees, depth 6, learning rate 0.05, minimum child weight 1, L2 1. Sensitivity: 1200 trees, depth 4, learning rate 0.03, minimum child weight 50, L2 5. Main and sensitivity fits sample 80% of rows and allow all columns; each setting uses three fitting seeds. Points: reported paired mean differences, with equal meter weight. Lines: unadjusted 95% bootstrap bounds from 2,000 whole-calendar-month draws and one common seed per draw. The bootstrap bounds do not describe a seed-averaged estimator or uncertainty when forecasting new meters. A draw omits a meter if none of its supported months was drawn; support is in the appendix. All seven families were chosen post hoc; comparisons share months and are subject to multiplicity. Differences do not isolate causal effects of individual inputs. Absolute losses, support, and the separate equal-month t-intervals are in the appendix. These results use frozen radiation revision 0f094c3, not merged 01ddf53. No deployment or feature adoption recommendation is established. Fair CRPS is the deciding loss for these matched 51-point ensembles; secondary loss metrics and lead-band robustness are reported separately.'
text.tspan: Power forecasts at six solar and three wind farms in National Grid Electricity Distribution's Lincolnshire trial
area each contain 51 weather-driven predictions. Fair continuous ranked probability score (fair CRPS) measures
their distributional error against observed power; lower is better. The comparisons match the same forecast cases
and were added after the original results.
Each row is the first recipe minus the second; negative means lower loss for the first. Each farm's effective
capacity is the 99th percentile of absolute observed power over its available history, including readings after
validation, not a connection rating. Loss is divided by that fixed scale for scoring only; one point is 1% of
capacity.
PV means photovoltaic. Numbers name real inputs: PV 2 uses temperature and short-wave radiation; PV 11 adds weather
and solar geometry. Wind 5 uses temperature, speeds, and directions at 10/100 m. Direction is the angle the wind
comes from, measured clockwise from north. Wind 9 adds eastward/northward velocity components (u/v) in m/s at both
heights; Wind 7 replaces each direction angle with its sine and cosine.
Full 24 is the cleaned full-input control; old lean Wind retains 16 inputs. Corrected wind/radiation processing and
per-meter squared-error fitting are shared. All retained sets duplicate their own inputs to width 24. Wind
representations use the same corrected polar inputs, not native upstream u/v, and add no weather information.
A trains April 2024–June 2025, tests July 2025–June 2026. Retrospective B trains July 2025–June 2026, tests April
2024–June 2025; its later training conditions the comparison.
Main: 500 trees, depth 6, learning rate 0.05, minimum child weight 1, L2 1. Sensitivity: 1200 trees, depth 4,
learning rate 0.03, minimum child weight 50, L2 5. Main and sensitivity fits sample 80% of rows and allow all
columns; each setting uses three fitting seeds.
Points: reported paired mean differences, with equal meter weight. Lines: unadjusted 95% bootstrap bounds from
2,000 whole-calendar-month draws and one common seed per draw. The bootstrap bounds do not describe a seed-averaged
estimator or uncertainty when forecasting new meters. A draw omits a meter if none of its supported months was
drawn; support is in the appendix.
All seven families were chosen post hoc; comparisons share months and are subject to multiplicity. Differences do
not isolate causal effects of individual inputs. Absolute losses, support, and the separate equal-month t-intervals
are in the appendix.
These results use frozen radiation revision 0f094c3, not merged 01ddf53. No deployment or feature adoption
recommendation is established.
Fair CRPS is the deciding loss for these matched 51-point ensembles; secondary loss metrics and lead-band
robustness are reported separately.
